title: Defensive retry profiles, id-key heuristics, and retryable error taxonomy (cross-SDK playbook)
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Background: We need a single cross-language guidance and default config set for client SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) that balances reliability, cost, and UX for both request/response and streaming paths. Existing SDKs have grown divergent: some clients aggressively retry on 5xx and 429 with tight backoffs, others are conservative. Streaming resume semantics are inconsistent which leads to duplicate consumptions or silent data loss in edge failures.

Scope: This ticket is the canonical playbook + implementation plan for three deliverables: 1) a small set of defensible retry profiles (e.g., conservative, default, aggressive) with numeric defaults for attempts, base jittered backoff, and token/latency budgets; 2) idempotency-key heuristics and recommended placement (request-level vs streaming chunk resume) plus server-compatible key formats; 3) a retryable-error taxonomy mapping transport, service, and inference-specific errors to retry policies (immediate retry, backoff-ok, non-retriable, resumable-with-idkey).

Goals: Provide language-agnostic rules, concrete examples for Python/TS/Go, migration guidance for existing customers, test harnesses (simulated transient errors and preemption), and telemetry signals for automatic profile adjustments later. Emphasize safety for stateful operations (file uploads, tool calls) and low risk of duplication for chat/completion workloads.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Three named retry profiles defined with numeric defaults and rationale (conservative/default/aggressive)
A2: Idempotency key spec: format, lifetime recommendations, where to set in SDKs, and server contract notes
A3: Error taxonomy: mapping of common service and transport errors to retry decision and suggested backoff parameters
A4: Example snippets for Python, TypeScript, and Go showing usage of profiles and id-key flow for both unary and streaming requests
A5: End-to-end integration tests in CI that inject 429/503/connection-close/stream-reset and validate no double-delivery beyond dedupe window
A6: Docs PR and SDK PRs opened with cross-language consistency checks and changelog entries
decision_log: 2026-02-21: Chose to expose a small set of opinionated profiles rather than surface dozens of knobs. Rationale: ease of adoption and predictable billing/latency.
2026-02-28: Agree to default to conservative profile for new tenants and opt-in aggressive for high-throughput customers.
2026-03-03: Streaming resume will use a two-part id-key: session id + chunk index fingerprint. Server will accept id-keys up to 128 bytes. This balances resumability with dedupe practicality.

2026-03-08: Decided against automatic transparent retries for operations that include side-effecting tool calls; SDK should surface retryable hint but require explicit developer consent via 'safe_retry' flag.

2026-03-11: Backoff defaults: base 200ms, max 5s, jitter=full; conservative attempts=2, default=4, aggressive=8. Token-budget aware early-abort added to prevent runaway costs on long-generation requests.
notes: 2026-02-22: Spike completed to model cost/latency tradeoffs for different attempt counts using production traces (sampled 10k requests). Results attached: https://go.redwood-internal/notes/retry-spike-2026
2026-02-26: Proto spec drafted and shared with SDK leads. Feedback requested from @Marta (TS), @Akira (Go), @Daniel (Python).
2026-03-02: Implemented local test harness that simulates preemption + intermittent 503s for streaming. Early findings: naive resume without index leads to up to 2x duplicates in 3% of runs.
2026-03-10: Began SDK PR for TypeScript with profile API: RedwoodClient.withRetryProfile('default'|'conservative'|'aggressive'). Open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-ts/pull/912
2026-03-12: Drafted docs and migration guide in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/Defensive+Retries+Playbook

implementation_plan: Step 1: Finalize numeric defaults and write formal spec (this ticket)
Step 2: Update SDKs with a small public API for profiles and id-key helpers; include examples and tiny migration helpers
Step 3: Add CI fault-injection tests for each SDK and add telemetry events to platform to distinguish retried vs original requests
Step 4: Docs PR and customer-facing migration guide; announce changes in SDK release notes
Step 5: Follow-up: runtime feature to emit 'retry_reason' telemetry and an opt-in auto-tune feature in Optimize
example_snippets:
PYTHON: with RetryProfile('default') as client:
    resp = client.completions.create(prompt=..., idempotency_key=make_idkey(session='chat-123', index=0))

TS: const client = new RedwoodClient({retryProfile: 'conservative'});
for await (const chunk of client.chat.stream({prompt, idempotencyKey: idKey})) { /* handle */ }

GO: ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 30*time.Second); defer cancel();
resp, err := client.Completions.Create(ctx, opts.WithRetryProfile(sdk.RetryDefault).WithIdKey(idKey))
risks: Duplicate responses in streaming if id-key granularity is wrong; mitigated by chunk-index fingerprint and short dedupe window (server-side)
Customer confusion if defaults change mid-account; mitigation: opt-in aggressive only, default conservative for newly created accounts, migration docs
Billing surprises if aggressive profile used with long tokens; mitigation: token-budget early-abort and SDK warning logs
